subject: Temporary subprocessor bridge for EU cutover - evidence & approvals requested
body:
From: Sven Muller <sven@cloudbridge.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: Temporary subprocessor bridge for EU cutover

Hi Priyom,

We have a short notice request from our engineering team: during a planned migration of our log processing pipeline on 2026-12-15, CloudBridge needs to spin up a short-lived processor in the EU region that will temporarily handle log forwarding for two weeks while we cut over. The component only forwards anonymized operational logs (no PII), and will not persist raw request payloads.

Can Redwood accept CloudBridge as a temporary subprocessor for that limited window? If yes, we can provide the roster and evidence packages. Questions we know you typically need:
- Exact data categories and sample fields we will forward
- Encryption at rest and in transit (we use TLS 1.3 and AES-256 at rest)
- KMS/HSM integration for keys and whether we can use your KMS or bring our own
- Residency guarantees and egress controls for the two-week window
- SOC2 / ISO certifications and point-in-time audit evidence
- Proposed SLA for handling incident response during cutover

Attaching a short spec sheet and we can upload the roster and a dataflow diagram on request. Please let us know the checklist items Redwood needs to greenlight a temporary subprocessor like this.

Thanks,
Sven Muller
Head of Integrations
CloudBridge
Attachment: temp_subprocessor_spec_sheet.pdf

-----
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Sven Muller <sven@cloudbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 14:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Temporary subprocessor bridge for EU cutover

Sven — thanks for the heads up.

High level: we may permit a timebound temporary subprocessor for operational logs, but we need the following before we can approve:
1) A one-sheet subprocessor roster (names, sub-roles, country of processing).
2) A dataflow diagram showing ingress point, redaction/anonymization step, where logs land, and any downstream exports.
3) Evidence of encryption at rest for the EU instance and confirmation of TLS in transit (cert fingerprints / cipher suites are fine).
4) Confirmation on KMS approach: will CloudBridge host keys or do you expect Redwood to manage rotation?
5) SOC2 Type II report or attestation for the last 12 months (can be redacted to remove unrelated controls).
6) A signed temporary addendum (DocuSign) listing dates, controls, and the option to terminate immediately on discovery of misconfiguration.
7) Contact for incident escalation and an SLA for responding to data incidents during the window.

Kimberly — looped in to confirm legal/DPA checklist; Naomi, FYI for residency/export implications.

Once we receive items 1–3 we can run a quick mapping and provide a go/no-go within 24 business hours. If anything contains PII we will need a bit more time.

Best,
Priyom
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

-----
From: Sven Muller <sven@cloudbridge.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@cloudbridge.com
Date: Wed, 09 Dec 2026 16:27:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Temporary subprocessor bridge for EU cutover

Thanks — attaching the roster and dataflow diagram now. We confirm the logs are operational telemetry only: service timestamps, request latencies, anonymized status codes; no user content or PII.

Attachments: CB-temp-roster-v1.xlsx, dataflow_cb_cutover.png
Shared link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_example_cutover_docs

KMS: CloudBridge will manage the EU instance keys in our tenant KMS (we can provide key rotation policy and access list). On encryption in transit, we use TLS 1.3; we can supply cert chain if needed. SOC2: we can provide the redacted Type II attestation — contracts@cloudbridge.com will send it to your secure upload.

We propose these dates: 2026-12-15 00:00 UTC start, 2026-12-29 23:59 UTC end. We also propose an immediate-localization fallback: if Redwood needs us to stop exporting any logs outside the EU during the window, we can restrict egress and only keep logs within EU data stores.

Please confirm whether temporary approval is feasible and which format you prefer for the addendum (DocuSign vs. signed PDF).

Cheers,
Sven

-----
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Temporary subprocessor bridge for EU cutover — please review

Naomi / Kimberly — forwarding the attachments CloudBridge just uploaded. Quick asks:
- Naomi: please confirm export-control / residency risk for a two-week EU-only processor that CloudBridge manages. Is the proposed localization fallback sufficient?
- Kimberly: please advise if a short-term DPA addendum with emergency termination clause is acceptable and whether Legal prefers DocuSign or countersigned PDF for speed.

I also want to flag we should run a light-weight mapping against our prefix/KV cache policies to ensure no application-level keys or KV caches are accidentally forwarded. If approved, I will raise the DocuSign template request and add the temporary subprocessor to our roster for that timebound window.

Thanks — will hold on approvals until I hear back.

Priyom
Senior Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
